lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.19 - A Fill in the blanks

details: Fill in the blanks reviews prior learning and checks comprehension as students recall the jobs and job action keywords they have learnt.
Look for confident recall, correct sentence structures and spelling.
“Do you want to go to the future? I do! Look at the pictures. Can you tell me the jobs? Let's listen carefully to the children... what do they want to be?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.19 - B. Listen and choose

details: Listen and choose practises listening skills and checks comprehension by asking students to select which job image matches the audio they hear.
Look for careful listening and confident and correct choices.
“Do we all want to have different jobs? Help me listen to these friends and find out what they want to be.”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.73 - A Find and write

details: Find and write asks students to recall prior learning to match each description with a picture and job.
Look for confident matching, correct spelling and careful penmanship.
“Do you know that I can see the future? It's true! But I can't see everything. I can only see some shapes.. Can you look at the pictures and tell me what they are?'”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.73 - B Read and circle

details: Read and circle tests students on the grammar they have covered in the unit, including their understanding of interrogative pronouns, infinitive verbs and verbs in the third person present tense.
Look for correct choices and note any errors and misconceptions, particularly if repeated.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - Presentation Think about your dream job. Then draw and fill in the chart. Present your dream job to the class.

details: The presentation task gives students a chance to apply their learning to themselves, choosing their own dream job, what they will do and who they want to work for.
Look for confident presentations, with clear pronunciation and correct sentence structures and word choices.
“It’s your turn now! Think about your future... in 20 years, who do you want to be? A film star? An astronaut? What about a teacher? Share your dream with the class!”
